- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% from prior 3-day avg), model often overshoots; cap next 3-day forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.25) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 2–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when sentiment is neutral or negative; reduce forecast by 3–5% for days 20–30.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+10% above 18-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.75) correlate with model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 5–8% if sentiment >0.75 in last 3 days.
